correctness.rationale: An untreated plant of degree d is lost with probability q^d, so guaranteeing any neighbor saves it with that probability; the true marginal is q times the normalized ranking score. When at most four plants contribute to a pairwise difference, one-versus-many signs have at most one crossing; two-plus/two-minus signs with at most two variations have at most one interior zero since q=1 is a zero; three variations force alternating unit monomials of strictly constant sign. No A-B-A crossing is possible. The five-plant seven-pollinator construction gives normalized scores 1+2q^5 and 2q for the only contenders and a uniquely minimized difference with two roots. Seven algebraic score checks and 21 independent exact rational state-enumeration checks passed using packaged verify.py. Restrictions q in (0,1), unit weights, single guarantee and distinct finite species are explicit.

value.rationale: An exact smallest plant count for reversible conservation priority is a natural structural boundary, and the constructive witness shows the management policy can switch away from and back to a higher-degree pollinator as uncertainty changes. The nontrivial four-term sign barrier and five-term attainment organize a potentially misleading ecological degree-priority heuristic; the exact cutoff is not an arbitrary table entry. Scope is explicitly limited to the simple static expected-richness model.
